metadata.description: x86-64 (ubuntu-latest) regression baseline. baseline_value IS the measured SLOW-CLASS median; tolerance_percent a uniform 45. Derivation: the floor is the SLOW-class median, so a fast-class assignment can only produce a positive delta and the 1.45x fleet spread cannot by itself justify any downward tolerance — an earlier version of this note derived the number from that spread, which does not follow. What the tolerance must absorb is downward excursion on the slow class: the per-primitive spread recorded in calibration_evidence is small (worst case hkdf_derive, median 131,341 vs min 123,672 = 5.8%), and the binding observation is the single 33% contention burst seen during the 2026-08 calibration on a shared runner. 45% is that burst plus margin. It is deliberately coarse: a regression smaller than 45% is not caught on this lane, which is why the homogeneous ubuntu-24.04-arm lane (arm-baseline.json, tolerance 15-25) is the precision gate and this one is a safety net. This lane is an honest coarse safety net; the homogeneous ubuntu-24.04-arm lane (arm-baseline.json, tolerance 15-25) is the precision gate. Updates require line-item justification per benchmarks/check_baseline_justification.py.

baseline_change_log.reason: Recalibrated to 65% of current measured performance (1,017 ops/sec measured on ubuntu-latest, see benchmark-results.json 2026-04-21T01:06:23Z). ML-DSA-65 signing is rejection-sampling based and its throughput on shared CI runners varies significantly with rejection rate for a fixed message; the v2.1.2 baseline of 1,918 ops/sec was measured on a less-loaded runner. No code regression: ML-DSA-65 keygen (2,951 ops/sec) and verify (6,322 ops/sec) both show -52% and -47% deltas (faster than baseline) on the same run, confirming the sign-side number is a runner-variance recalibration, not a C-level slowdown. 35% regression headroom preserved via the `tolerance_percent: 40` entry.

Re-floored after observing stable runner-variance on a slower contended sandbox host (3-run medians taken with build configured at -DAMA_ENABLE_AVX512=ON; AVX-512 SHA3 4-way kernel landed in this release). Each baseline set to ~65% of the slowest-runner stable median so even a contended GitHub-hosted shared runner clears the regression threshold without false positives; canonical Sapphire Rapids / Zen 4 hosts continue to clear by a wide negative-regression margin (faster than baseline). full_package_create tolerance bumped 50%→70% to absorb the GC-stall variance observed at 3-run min/max ratios > 2.5x. README, benchmark-report.md, and wiki/Performance-Benchmarks.md continue to publish the canonical-host throughput numbers — those are distinct from this regression floor, which is the worst-case-runner safety net. Source measurements: stable-medians captured 2026-04-25 across 30+ runs of validation_suite.py and 10+ runs of benchmark_runner.py; full_package_verify floor lowered 2044→700 to absorb the borderline 47–55% variance band. Source measurements: 3-run medians captured 2026-04-25, full transcript saved alongside benchmark-results.json on the consolidate branch.

baseline_change_log.change: Re-floored every entry that had drifted. The floors were measured against v2.1.2 and declared valid through v3.0.0 while the library shipped 3.4.0, and nothing enforced that window, so the regression job was comparing today's code against four-release-old numbers: ML-DSA-65 signing carried 27.4x headroom and full-package creation 23.0x, meaning a 96% regression would still have reported PASS. New floors are 0.65 * min(measured, canonical benchmark-report.md), per the project's documented 35%-headroom convention, and no floor was lowered. secp256k1 signing additionally reflects the fixed-base comb landed in this branch (2,545 -> 7,966 ops/s raw C). Enforced going forward by tests/test_benchmark_baseline_freshness.py. Measured on: container, Linux x86-64, 4 cores, gcc 13, `python benchmarks/benchmark_runner.py` and `./build/bin/benchmark_c_raw`.

Every `baseline_value` in this file is carried forward unchanged; only `applies_through_release` moved. Rationale: of the primitives this file floors, 4.0.0 touches exactly one measured path — Ed25519 verify and point decode gain `ama_ed25519_point_y_is_canonical`, a single branch-free 32-byte comparison per decode, against a verify costing ~10^5 ns. No other floored primitive changed — ed25519_keygen, ed25519_sign, ed25519_verify, secp256k1_ecdsa_sign, secp256k1_ecdsa_verify, ama_sha3_256_hash, hmac_sha3_256, hkdf_derive, dilithium_keygen, dilithium_sign, dilithium_verify, kyber_keygen, kyber_encapsulate, aes_256_gcm_encrypt, chacha20poly1305_encrypt, x25519_scalarmult, full_package_create and full_package_verify all keep their existing floors. AUTHORITY: these floors were NOT re-measured for this entry. The canonical measurement is the benchmark-regression CI job, which runs on the calibrated runner class named in `system` and gates this PR. A local run on a non-canonical contended sandbox VM (`./build/bin/benchmark_c_raw`) recorded 6965 ops/sec for Ed25519 verify, 25702 for sign and 28185 for keygen; those sit below the 13000/33000/31000 floors purely because that host is slower than the canonical class, so they corroborate nothing and are recorded only so the numbers are not mistaken for a calibration. If the benchmark-regression job fails on this PR, these floors need a genuine canonical re-measure, not a further window extension.

KEYGEN FLOORS RE-MEASURED FOR INVARIANT-41 (PR #391): key generation now includes the FIPS 140-3 pairwise consistency test on every keypair — a sign+verify for signature keys, an encapsulate+decapsulate for KEM keys — so the keygen benchmarks measure keygen-plus-PCT, deliberately: hiding the test from the benchmark would report a cost users do not get. Floors are set to the canonical benchmark-regression CI job's measurements on the PCT-bearing head (commit f195e69): ed25519_keygen 31000 -> 12651 ops/sec, dilithium_keygen 2100 -> 1281 ops/sec, kyber_keygen 3400 -> 3158 ops/sec. Only ed25519_keygen, dilithium_keygen and kyber_keygen change; no other primitive's measured path was touched by INVARIANT-41 (x25519_scalarmult and the secp256k1/sign/verify/encrypt benches do not generate keys). FULL RECALIBRATION FROM THE REPAIRED HARNESS (PR #394). baseline_value becomes the measured median (slow-class median for x86) and tolerance_percent the single derived allowance — see description. Every primitive changed; per-primitive from/to values with measurements and runner identifiers are in the recalibration commit message and in calibration_evidence.per_primitive. baseline_source_release advances to 4.0.0, making the freshness window honest for the first time since 2026-05-15 (ARM) / 2026-07-29 (x86).

WINDOW EXTENDED TO 5.0.0, NO FLOOR CHANGES. The 5.0.0 major bump pushes the package past `applies_through_release` (4.0.0) and would trip test_benchmark_baseline_freshness. Every `baseline_value` in this file is carried forward unchanged; only `applies_through_release` moves. Rationale: these floors ARE the 2026-08-14 full recalibration recorded in the previous entry — measured in this same PR (#394) from the repaired harness on the canonical benchmark-regression runner class for this file (ubuntu-latest, x86_64) — and 5.0.0 is cut from the tree those medians describe. The only commits between the recalibration head and the 5.0.0 cut are: the CodeQL alert cleanup (an error-path log line in `keypair_generate`'s ctypes guard, import-style unification), the polynomial-regex (ReDoS) hardening in three tools/ gate scripts (no shipped code path), the fail-closed unreadable-candidate rule in library discovery (load-time, not per-operation), the binding-extension digest signing (build- and import-time), CI probe and C-test-lane fixes, documentation and CHANGELOG restructuring, and the version bump itself. Code the floors describe DID change after they were measured, and this entry no longer claims otherwise: the Kyber barrett_reduce rewrite (an NTT inner-loop function), the ChaCha20-Poly1305 post-verify control flow, the dispatch auto-tune sentinel, a SHA3 squeeze-entry guard, and the benchmark harness itself all landed after the calibration head. Each is itemised with its reasoning in metadata.floor_drift_acknowledged, which benchmarks/check_baseline_justification.py now verifies against `git diff` from the calibration commit — the previous sentence here asserted the opposite and nothing checked it. The floors are therefore carried as a coarse safety net that describes a very slightly older tree, not as a measurement of the shipped one — the same tree-delta argument as the 3.5.0 and 4.0.0 window extensions above, this time with floors measured inside the same PR rather than carried forward from an earlier release. If that job fails on this PR, the floors need a genuine canonical re-measure, not a further window extension.

ED25519 FLOORS RE-MEASURED UPWARD on the in-house backend. The vendored ed25519-donna backend was removed in PR #394's twenty-first maintenance pass and replaced by the in-house radix-2^51 backend, which the benchmark-regression job on the canonical runner class for this file (ubuntu-latest (x86_64)) measures faster on every Ed25519 row at head c6020ac: ed25519_keygen 10822 -> 16751 ops/sec, ed25519_sign 53885 -> 77991 ops/sec, ed25519_verify 19181 -> 32019 ops/sec. baseline_value is the measurement from that job (the file's convention: baseline_value IS the measured value on the canonical runner); tolerance_percent is unchanged and absorbs run-to-run variance. ED25519 FLOORS RE-BASED TO FOUR-RUN MEDIANS on the canonical runner class for this file (ubuntu-latest (x86_64)). The preceding entry set the three Ed25519 floors from ONE benchmark-regression job at head c6020ac. The four jobs that followed on byte-identical Ed25519 code (heads f2ac1d8, 4a45408, 755cd22 and 447cdf0 change no Ed25519 source; run/job 34070019745/101585569464, 34082980156/101621669890, 34084425292/101625629987, 34084821515/101626784285) measured ed25519_keygen 16622 / 14436 / 16304 / 14349; ed25519_sign 73660 / 67625 / 73366 / 67521; ed25519_verify 33234 / 28003 / 32777 / 28306 ops/sec. baseline_value is now the median of those four (even count: mean of the middle two, rounded to the nearest integer; computed by script from the job logs, not by hand): ed25519_keygen 16751 -> 15370 ops/sec, ed25519_sign 77991 -> 70496 ops/sec, ed25519_verify 32019 -> 30542 ops/sec. tolerance_percent stays 45. The ubuntu-latest fleet is two-class and the c6020ac sample was a fast-class one. With the tolerance unchanged the effective minimum (floor x 55/100) moves 9213 -> 8454, 42895 -> 38773, 17610 -> 16798 ops/sec; the slowest of the four runs sits 6.6% / 4.2% / 8.3% below the new floors and clears the new minimums by 70% / 74% / 67%, and it is still above the removed ed25519-donna backend's last measurement on this runner class (11855 / 59847 / 21322 ops/sec) on every row. No other floor moves; calibration_evidence and floor_drift_acknowledged are unchanged.

ed25519_sign FLOOR RE-BASED 70496 -> 38170 ops/sec for a DELIBERATE, documented slowdown: INVARIANT-51 makes ama_ed25519_sign derive A = [a]B and refuse a secret key whose stored public half disagrees, which adds a second fixed-base scalar multiplication to every signature. The old floor no longer described the code, and the benchmark-regression job was FAILING on it -- measured +45.37% against a 45% tolerance, i.e. not a flake but a deterministic red. A floor exists to catch an UNINTENDED regression; one left in place after an intended change is a broken alarm, and the choice is to restore the speed or to move the floor. The speed cannot be restored without either removing the check (the private-scalar recovery hazard it closes, see INVARIANT-51) or caching key-derived material in long-lived storage, which trades a documented cost for an undocumented INVARIANT-6 one. So the floor moves. DERIVATION, host-independent rather than measured on a development host: the ratio is taken from this tree at the C level, min-of-20000 medians with the binding excluded -- ama_ed25519_sign 12586 ns before the check and 23245 ns after, and ama_ed25519_point_from_scalar (the added operation, on its own) 10659 ns; 23245/12586 = 1.8469x. Both multiplications scale together on any microarchitecture, so the ratio carries across hosts where an absolute number would not. Applied to the canonical runner's own four-run median of 70496 from the preceding entry: 70496 / 1.8469 = 38170. Cross-check against that entry's full observed range on ubuntu-latest (x86_64), 67521..73660 ops/sec, the post-change band is 36559..39883, so the 45% tolerance leaves the failure point at 20994 -- far below the worst run the canonical runner has ever produced. tolerance_percent is deliberately NOT changed: the regression is accounted for in baseline_value, and widening the band as well would hide the next regression behind this one. ed25519_keygen and ed25519_verify are untouched; verify gains the two INVARIANT-48 small-order byte predicates at +0.7% and needs no re-base.

FIVE x86_64 FLOORS RE-BASED TO FOUR-RUN MEDIANS on the canonical runner class for this file (ubuntu-latest (x86_64)), replacing the values the 2026-09 audit remediation left behind. Source: the Benchmark Regression Detection (x86_64) jobs of CI runs 35545407750 (job 106170292775, head ebc80b9), 35548705329 (job 106179299451, head 1bf806b), 35608144468 (job 106360245063, head da8901d) and 35611329428 (job 106370902549, head 1e79cd1), 2026-09-20 to 2026-09-21, none of which changes a measured path. Run 35548705329 is a fast-class sample on every row (20-45% above the other three), which is the two-class fleet the 2026-08-14 recalibration documents; the medians are therefore slow-class medians. tolerance_percent stays 45 on every row: the changes are accounted for in baseline_value, and widening the band as well would hide the next regression behind these. Effective minimums (floor x 0.55) move 8454 -> 6802, 20994 -> 21346, 16798 -> 15364, 1091 -> 1021 and 1893 -> 1544 ops/sec, and the slowest of the four runs clears each new minimum by at least 79%. The other fourteen floors are unchanged: all four runs measured above every one of them on this runner class (the full per-row table is in docs/BENCHMARK_HISTORY.md, 2026-09-22). calibration_evidence still names the 2026-08-14 multi-run calibration for those rows; floor_drift_acknowledged carries the provenance-only change to benchmarks/benchmark_runner.py made in the same pass.

ed25519_sign_expanded ROW ADDED at a DERIVED floor of 61671 ops/sec (ubuntu-latest (x86_64)), not a measured one: this row is new and the canonical runner has not run it. Derivation, host-independent in kind: the row times Ed25519SigningKey.sign, which is ama_ed25519_sign_expanded (one fixed-base scalar multiplication plus a two-compression SHA-512 tag check) where ed25519_sign is ama_ed25519_sign (two fixed-base multiplications, INVARIANT-51's per-call derivation). Measured on the development host on 2026-09-22 (Intel Xeon @2.80GHz, 4 vCPU container, taskset -c 0, the runner's own harness, three runs then a full snapshot run at 24341f8): ed25519_sign 34566 / 34977 / 34713 / 34900 and ed25519_sign_expanded 55524 / 55607 / 55728 / 55465 ops/sec, ratios 1.606 / 1.590 / 1.605 / 1.589. The snapshot run's record was superseded the same day by the re-run at 4e4fa7f that the tree now carries (benchmarks/benchmark-results.json: ed25519_sign 35287, ed25519_sign_expanded 56746, ratio 1.608), so its two figures live only in this entry; at the C level (build/bin/benchmark_c_raw, median of 1000) ama_ed25519_sign 24780 ns against ama_ed25519_sign_expanded 13613 ns, 1.820x, the Python ratio being lower by the fixed ctypes cost each signature carries. The LOWEST of the five Python ratios, 1.589, applied to this file's ed25519_sign floor: 38811 x 1.589 = 61671 -- the conservative choice, since a floor derived from a lower ratio can only be easier to clear. tolerance_percent 45 as for its sibling, so the failure point is 33919 -- below the ed25519_sign row itself. Re-base to the canonical runner's own median once it has run this row; a derived floor is a placeholder for a measurement, not a substitute.

ama_sha3_256_hash.description: AMA native C SHA3-256 hashing of 1KB data (FIPS 202, ctypes)

ed25519_keygen.description: Ed25519 key pair generation through the Python API: one CSPRNG seed draw + native keygen + the FIPS 140-3 pairwise-consistency sign/verify that keypair() runs on every key (native keygen alone is about a sixth of the timed operation). Not comparable with the 4.x native-keygen-only row.

ed25519_sign.description: Ed25519 signature generation through the Python API with the 64-byte seed || A key (native C); INVARIANT-51 re-derives A = [a]B on every call. The once-at-load form is the ed25519_sign_expanded row.

ed25519_sign_expanded.description: Ed25519 signature generation through Ed25519SigningKey: the key is loaded once, outside the timed operation, with the INVARIANT-51 derivation of the public half done at load; each timed signature re-checks the expanded form's tag (ama_ed25519_sign_expanded) instead of re-deriving. Same 240-byte message and key source as ed25519_sign; the ratio between the two rows is the per-signature cost the derivation had.

secp256k1_ecdsa_sign.description: secp256k1 ECDSA signing (native C, RFC 6979 deterministic nonce)

secp256k1_ecdsa_verify.description: secp256k1 ECDSA verification (native C, Shamir's-trick joint multiply, low-s + canonical-pubkey policy)

x25519_scalarmult.description: X25519 single-shot Diffie-Hellman scalar-mult (native C, default dispatch). Backed by fe64 (radix-2^64, MULX/ADX) on x86-64 hosts with BMI2+ADX, fe51 (radix-2^51) on 64-bit hosts without, and gf16 on 32-bit. The AVX2 4-way kernel is OPT-IN via AMA_DISPATCH_USE_X25519_AVX2=1 and is intentionally not faster than scalar fe64 on MULX/ADX hosts — see src/c/dispatch/ama_dispatch.c:478-502 and tests/test_x25519_dispatch_policy.py for the dispatch contract. Re-floored 5,000 → 13,000 (2026-04-27 audit) so the regression gate actually catches a >40% drop from canonical-host throughput rather than ignoring it.

x25519_scalarmult_batch4.description: X25519 batch-4 Diffie-Hellman under default dispatch — measures BATCHES/SEC, not per-op rate. On MULX/ADX hosts this is roughly x25519_scalarmult / 4 plus the wrapper's per-batch overhead (canonical-host run measured ~4,100 batches/sec vs ~17,000 single-shot ops/sec). A significantly slower batches/sec number typically means the AVX2 4-way kernel was accidentally selected as the default — that is a regression on every shipped Broadwell+/Zen+ part (see PR #273 design note and ama_dispatch.c:478-502). The runner calls native_x25519_scalarmult_batch with count=4 so this baseline genuinely exercises the batch wrapper, not four sequential native_x25519_key_exchange calls.
